eyebrow: San Francisco employment and community support · Emergency peer response
program: Conditional whole-organization value of a $100,000 unrestricted gift

nutshell.headline: Community ambassadors can help people through emergencies. The extra health created by the next gift is unmeasured.
nutshell.body: Our conditional central estimate is $1.97 million per 10 SF-resident QALYs. A joint favorable stress reaches $45,762, but a strong public baseline is $17.70 million. These scenarios are not confidence bounds or a current funding offer.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: Code Tenderloin's current ambassadors and Night Navigators assist drug-related emergencies and recovery access. Timely overdose response has a credible causal mechanism.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: Marginal gift allocation, unique high-risk reach, sustained response coverage and complete delivery costs are analyst judgments. City-funded and partner services are already part of the counterfactual.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: No verified costed additional cohort or $100,000 peer-response funding offer.

summary.label: Central donor USD / 10 QALYs
summary.detail: Same full gift in each nested geography. SF 90% and Bay 98% of US modeled health are residence priors, not measured service shares.

summary.label: Whole-gift boundary
summary.detail: 25% modeled peer-response allocation; 75% other work and overhead retains its cost with unquantified health. No promise that the organization allocates this way.

summary.label: Current recipient
summary.detail: Official site and current IRS record agree. Former sponsor Center for New Music is a different recipient; legacy contract transfer is not presumed.

summary.label: Central gross resource envelope
summary.detail: Adds a judgmental public/partner supply allowance outside donor cash. This is not net societal cost; future medical care and family time are omitted.

programSection.body: Code Tenderloin provides job readiness, training, youth and reentry support, casework, community events and outreach. The current ambassador page identifies drug-related emergency and recovery support; a September 1, 2026 DPH directory corroborates active barrier-removal services. This report quantifies only a prospective peer-response component of a general gift.

steps.title: Allocate the entire gift
steps.detail: All $100,000 remains in the cost numerator, including other programs and institutional overhead.

steps.title: Fund additional peer contact
steps.detail: Central $60 per worker-hour and six hours per unique offered person-year include repeated and unsuccessful contacts. These are complete direct-delivery judgments, not a priced offer.

steps.title: Change response beyond existing care
steps.detail: Only a remaining gap in timely rescue counts. SFAF, SFCHC, DPH and other peers are part of the baseline and cannot also claim the same patient-time.

steps.title: Count finite additional survival
steps.detail: Peer response changes fatal OD hazard for one service year. Later survivors face the same recurrent-overdose and competing mortality hazards as the comparison group.

programSection.boundary: No historical enrollment, referral, training credential or reported reversal is treated as a new life saved. Other clinical, employment, housing, art and policy impacts remain unquantified.

model.headline: One year of incremental response; finite additional alive-time
model.body: The central cohort is selected three months after the gift. We integrate the difference between survival curves for ten care-relative years, discounting at 3%. No additional response benefit is assumed after year one, and no full lifetime is repeatedly assigned to rescues of the same person.

equation.label: Whole-gift peer-response bridge
equation.expression: Offers = gift × peer allocation / [(hourly wage × payroll loading + direct nonwage delivery) × worker-hours per offered year]. Q = offers × financial additionality × (finite discounted survival difference × utility − shared harm) − independent harm.
equation.result: Central: 69.44 offered packages, 34.72 additional packages, 0.11676 extra people alive at service-year end, 0.564257 US QALYs and 0.507832 SF QALYs.

inputs.label: Peer-response allocation
inputs.basis: Marginal allocation is not inferred from the sponsor's historical expense mix; remaining portfolio and overhead cost stays.

inputs.label: Direct worker-hour cash / hours per offered person-year
inputs.confidence: Provider wage anchor plus cost judgments
inputs.basis: Official ambassador wage is about $27/hour; payroll loading and direct logistics/supervision are judgments. Count two workers as two worker-hours; include failed and repeated contacts.

inputs.label: Financial additionality
inputs.basis: Addresses funding replacement, separate from actual no-gift rescue availability. No verified private expansion offer.

inputs.label: Annual fatal OD / other death hazards
inputs.basis: Not risks for every program client. Constant hazards are not a fitted recovery or age-specific model; external survivor evidence cautions against full-lifetime rescue credit.

inputs.label: Residual addressable gap / effective timely response
inputs.basis: Includes witnessing, timing, uptake and partner overlap. Central remaining OD hazard falls 9%; no additional witness or adherence multiplier.

inputs.label: Utility / finite horizon
inputs.basis: Count extra alive-time once. Full-health utility sensitivity included; social status is not treated as human worth.

inputs.label: SF / Bay resident shares
inputs.basis: The same full gift is divided by regional health. Shares apply to harms as well and are not measured clinic-location fractions.

inputs.label: Other gross resources / shared harm per offer
inputs.range: Zero extra cost; null and independent-harm cases
inputs.basis: Resources are outside donor cash and count all offers, including replacement and failure. No net societal cost or savings claim.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: One-year health clipping is $38.11M/10 SF QALYs. Joint favorable $45,762 is not an established local bargain; strong public baseline is $17.70M. These are structural stresses, not fitted probabilities.
model.fundingBoundary: Independent EIN and current services are verified. Public CHOPP and ambassador funding remains baseline; the sponsor/direct contract split, complete current budget and marginal gift allocation are unresolved.

evidence.design: Current official provider, IRS and September 2026 DPH disclosures
evidence.population: Code Tenderloin services and current recipient
evidence.result: Standalone EIN and active barrier-removal/ambassador services supported.
evidence.transfer: Does not identify how many otherwise-fatal overdoses a general gift would prevent.

evidence.design: Coffin, Maya and Kahn 2022 decision model
evidence.result: Timely naloxone coverage reduces modeled fatal overdose risk; faster fentanyl progression constrains response.
evidence.transfer: Supports mechanism, not Code's actual residual access gap or response effect.

evidence.design: Weiner et al. 2020 Massachusetts retrospective survivor cohort
evidence.result: 5.5% died within one year, with substantial early mortality.
evidence.transfer: Requires recurrent/competing mortality treatment; not a contemporary SF parameter estimate.

evidence.design: FY2024 sponsor Form 990 and June 2025 CHOPP request
evidence.population: Historical sponsored project and planned public services
evidence.result: $4.77M historical Code program expenses; material prospective public funding described.
evidence.transfer: Not current standalone audited finances. Mixed CHOPP service units cannot become marginal cost per person.

reservations: No current complete independent budget or verified $100,000 marginal peer-response offer.
Ordinary gift allocation and complete direct-delivery package are constructed judgments.
Unique high-risk reach and sustained incremental response over a year are unmeasured.
Legacy sponsor contract transfer is not assumed; current public and partner services limit additionality.
Finite constant-risk health model does not fit recovery transitions or age-specific survival.
excludedBenefits: Medication-treatment enrollments and other clinical benefits
